summary: The article describes how adventure and obstacle races have become popular among local teenagers, building confidence, camaraderie, and resilience. It covers specific races, coaches and participants, professional training, obstacle design, inclusivity, school and environmental effects, and economic benefits to local businesses. It closes with plans for more races and possible scholarship programs next season.
one_line: Local adventure and obstacle races are boosting teenagers' confidence, community, and resilience while benefiting schools, trainers, and businesses.
key_facts: On Saturday, September 16, 2023, teenagers with numbered bibs gathered at Deer Valley Park for an adventure race.
Jenna Harrison, head coach at HighPeak Fitness, says the trend took off around late 2023 as teens sought an escape from digital saturation.
Jenna Harrison has trained over 200 young athletes for local obstacle events.
'The Savage Sprint' took place on October 5th and 'The Boulder Dash' on October 21st at Miller's Woods, drawing hundreds of teenagers.
Sixteen-year-old Ethan Torres completed the 5K 'Jungle Jaunt' on November 9, 2023, and said each obstacle is like a puzzle to solve on the go.
Fifteen-year-old Mia Rodriguez said at the 'Urban Warrior Challenge' on December 2 that racing teammates have become 'like a small family'.
Alex Strauss manages The Forge, a gym that developed specialized training programs for adventure racing to reduce injuries and teach correct technique.
Christina Nguyen, a mechanical engineer, volunteered at the 'Peak Pursuit' on September 30 and praised the safety and calculated design of obstacles.
Jaden Lee, a high school sophomore, says adventure racing is inclusive because everyone has their own strengths.
Local schools have begun incorporating elements of obstacle training into physical education curricula.
Races promote 'leave no trace' conservation practices and teach racers about local flora and fauna.
Carlos Mendez, manager of 'The Trailhead' café overlooking the Sentry Ridge racecourse, says race days are some of the café's busiest.
Plans include adding new races next season and possibly establishing scholarship programs for less privileged teens.
